newsitem.title: INDIA: Nuns end search for Mother Teresa's successor.
newsitem.headline: Nuns end search for Mother Teresa's successor.

text.p: Roman Catholic nuns have completed deliberations to select a successor for Mother Teresa at the head of the Missionaries of Charity religious order, a senior church official said on Thursday.

"Everything is over now," said the official, who on Thursday visited the order's headquarters in the eastern Indian city of Calcutta with Archbishop Henry D'Souza. He did not say who would succeed the 86-year-old Nobel Peace Prize winner.
The renowned missionary, suffering from heart, kidney and lung ailments, had said she did not want to continue to lead the order she founded in 1948.
The election of Mother Teresa's successor has been postponed twice since September. It was first set for September 8, but put off because Mother Teresa was ill.

More than 100 nuns from around the world then went into retreat on January 16 and had planned to vote in a secret ballot on February 2. But the order's electoral college, apparently unable to find a clear-cut successor, decided instead to hold closed-door deliberations before taking a vote.
Church officials had said the order might opt to set up a committee of senior nuns to lead it rather than name just one successor to Mother Teresa.
